newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on high C. Bank rate.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on high C. Bank rate.

text.p: The Philippine peso recovered from speculative attacks on Monday after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate by six percentage points to a two-year high of 30 percent, traders said.

Speculators pounced on the peso in the morning, taking their cue from a Singapore newspaper which quoted Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo as saying the local currency may be devalued against the dollar. De Ocampo denied the report.
The peso ended at 26.397 to the dollar, up from the early deals of 26.40/26.401 and the previous day's 26.399.
